Q189.L1t: Procedural due process under the Fourteenth Amendment governs when a state must give notice and a hearing before it deprives a person of a protected interest.
Q189.L2t: Professional licenses that a person has already obtained are generally treated as protected property or liberty interests, so states may not revoke them without due process.
Q189.L3t: Due process requires a hearing only to resolve disputed facts, and here the conviction in a prior criminal trial with full procedural protections already established the facts that triggered the mandatory revocation.
Q189.L4t: The board can revoke the license without a further hearing because the criminal trial already determined the relevant facts, so a trial-type hearing would serve no purpose.
Q189.L2f: A medical license is only a revocable privilege, so the state may take it away at any time without any procedural protections.
Q189.L3f: The Constitution's full faith and credit clause requires every agency of a state to treat a state court judgment as binding, so a licensing board has no discretion to hold its own proceeding after a conviction.
Q189.L4f: The board should win because the full faith and credit clause obliges it to give effect to the conviction and revoke the license summarily.

Q190.L1t: The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination and the Miranda rules limit how police may obtain statements from people suspected of crimes.
Q190.L2t: The prosecution must prove by a preponderance of the evidence that a confession was voluntary before it can be admitted at trial.
Q190.L3t: Under due process, a confession obtained by coercion, threats, or other overbearing of the suspect's will is not the product of free choice and cannot be used as evidence.
Q190.L4t: A confession is inadmissible when the statement was involuntary.
Q190.L2f: Under current law, a confession is treated as voluntary and admissible so long as the suspect was physically unharmed, whatever other pressure police used.
Q190.L3f: Miranda protections apply only to statements made in response to police questioning, so a statement that was not a response to known interrogation is not admissible, whatever the circumstances.
Q190.L4f: A confession is inadmissible when it was not made in response to a known police interrogation.

Q191.L1t: Partnership law determines when people doing business together share responsibility for the business's debts to outsiders.
Q191.L2t: A lender who receives only repayment of a loan, with interest not measured by profits, is generally not a partner in the borrower's business.
Q191.L3t: A person who represents himself, or permits himself to be represented, as a partner is liable to any third party who extends credit in reasonable reliance on that representation.
Q191.L4t: Both Bob and Ted are liable to Pete, jointly, because Ted is a partner by estoppel.
Q191.L2f: A lender who accepts a reduced interest rate on a loan thereby becomes a co-owner of the business under partnership law.
Q191.L3f: A business operated under a partnership name creates a distinct legal entity, so the third-party creditor's claims are limited to the assets of that business and not those of the individuals.
Q191.L4f: Pete can recover only from the de facto partnership arising from the Wilson and Lamar relationship, and not from either man personally.

Q192.L1t: Criminal liability for helping with a crime is analyzed under common law doctrines of accomplice liability, conspiracy, and the elements of burglary and larceny.
Q192.L2t: At common law, conspiracy is an agreement between two or more persons to commit an unlawful act, and accomplice liability requires that the helper intend to aid the crime.
Q192.L3t: The friend only pretended to join and intended from the start to have the young man arrested, so he never truly agreed with the young man and never shared any purpose of seeing the theft succeed.
Q192.L4t: The friend is not guilty of any offense, because he lacked the genuine agreement and the intent to further the theft that conspiracy and accomplice liability require.
Q192.L2f: At common law, conspiracy is complete only when a participant takes a substantial overt act toward the crime, and mere words of agreement are never enough.
Q192.L3f: Under the common law, a person who drives a burglar to the scene and waits outside is a principal in the second degree, and his private motive for helping is irrelevant to liability.
Q192.L4f: The friend is guilty of burglary, because he drove the young man to the house and thereby became a participant in the break-in.

Q193.L1t: The Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment limits how state and local governments may treat different groups of people.
Q193.L2t: In Plyler v. Doe, the Supreme Court considered a state law that denied public education to children who were illegal aliens.
Q193.L3t: The Court has held that illegal aliens are not a suspect class and education is not a fundamental right, yet it still struck down a bar on schooling their children because it imposes a lifelong penalty on children who are not responsible for their status and does not substantially further a substantial state interest.
Q193.L4t: The ordinance is invalid because excluding undocumented children from school over an unpaid fee is not substantially related to an important governmental interest.
Q193.L2f: In Plyler v. Doe, the Supreme Court held that illegal aliens are a suspect class, so any law treating them differently must satisfy strict scrutiny.
Q193.L3f: The constitutional test for this fee turns on whether the extra cost of hiring bilingual teachers places an excessive financial burden on the school system, and the Equal Protection Clause is concerned with that burden.
Q193.L4f: The ordinance is invalid because requiring the school board to hire additional bilingual teachers places an undue burden on the public school system.

Q194.L1t: Contracts for the sale of goods are governed by the Uniform Commercial Code, which sets rules for delivery, acceptance, and remedies.
Q194.L2t: A C.O.D. term means the buyer pays on delivery, and the buyer here accepted and paid for the 490 widgets that were tendered.
Q194.L3t: Under the perfect tender rule, a seller must deliver exactly the quantity promised, so delivering 490 of 500 widgets is a failure to perform the contract as written, and the buyer's acceptance of part does not waive its claim for the shortfall.
Q194.L4t: The buyer will recover because the manufacturer did not deliver all 500 widgets it promised and so failed to perform its contractual obligation.
Q194.L2f: A C.O.D. shipping term means the seller bears all risk and may not be held liable for any quantity shortfall once the buyer has inspected the goods.
Q194.L3f: A breach of contract supports recovery only if the missing performance is so substantial that it defeats the essential purpose of the agreement, and a shortfall of two percent does not.
Q194.L4f: The buyer will recover because the manufacturer's failure to deliver the remaining widgets was a material breach of the contract.

Q195.L1t: Peak expiratory flow meters are simple handheld devices used to measure how fast a person can exhale air from the lungs.
Q195.L2t: Serial peak flow readings are typically taken morning and evening, often over about two weeks, to look for how much the measurements vary.
Q195.L3t: Diagnostic value comes from marked diurnal or day-to-day variability in airflow, which reflects reversible airway narrowing, a hallmark of one particular obstructive condition and not of fixed obstruction or infections.
Q195.L4t: Peak flow variation over two weeks is diagnostic in asthma.
Q195.L2f: Peak flow readings are always taken only once, in a clinic, and are never recorded at home over several days.
Q195.L3f: Fixed, progressive airflow obstruction in chronic smokers produces large day-to-day swings in peak flow, which is the defining feature used to diagnose that chronic lung disease.
Q195.L4f: Serial peak flow variation over two weeks is diagnostic in COPD.

Q196.L1t: Proteins are large biological macromolecules built from smaller units called amino acids and have many roles in living cells.
Q196.L2t: Amino acids join in a condensation reaction that releases a molecule of water as each new link in the chain forms.
Q196.L3t: The covalent link between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of the next is a carbon–nitrogen amide linkage that forms the backbone of the polypeptide chain.
Q196.L4t: Amino acids in a protein are linked by peptide bonds.
Q196.L2f: Amino acids are joined in a hydrolysis reaction that consumes water, and the polypeptide chain is made of identical repeating units.
Q196.L3f: The backbone of a protein is built from bonds formed by full electron transfer between oppositely charged amino acid side groups, creating charged attraction that holds the chain together.
Q196.L4f: Amino acids in a protein are linked by ionic bonds.

Q197.L1t: Dopamine is a catecholamine drug given by intravenous infusion, with dose rates commonly expressed per kilogram of body weight per minute.
Q197.L2t: Infusion calculations require converting between micrograms and milligrams, where 1 milligram equals 1000 micrograms, and between minutes and hours.
Q197.L3t: Multiply 4 micrograms by 65 kg to get the dose per minute, then multiply by 60 minutes, and divide the resulting micrograms by 1000 to convert to milligrams.
Q197.L4t: The person will receive 15.6 milligrams in an hour.
Q197.L2f: Dopamine infusion rates are always calculated in milligrams per kilogram per hour, so no unit conversion between micrograms and milligrams is ever needed.
Q197.L3f: To convert micrograms to milligrams you divide by 100, and the per-minute dose of 260 micrograms is then multiplied by 60 minutes.
Q197.L4f: The person will receive 156 milligrams in an hour.

Q198.L1t: Nucleic acids such as DNA and RNA are built from long chains of nucleotide units.
Q198.L2t: The genetic material of cells is a nucleic acid that is passed on from parent cells to daughter cells during division.
Q198.L3t: Genes are stored in the nucleic acid whose sugar is deoxyribose, which forms the double helix described by Watson and Crick.
Q198.L4t: Our genetic material is DNA, which stands for deoxyribonucleic acid.
Q198.L2f: The genetic material of human cells is stored mainly in the cytoplasm and is not passed on to daughter cells during division.
Q198.L3f: Nucleic acids contain nitrogen, and the name of the genetic molecule comes from a nitro group attached to each nucleotide in place of the phosphate.
Q198.L4f: Our genetic material is a dinitronucleic acid, so that is the correct answer.

Q199.L1t: Abnormal breath sounds heard with a stethoscope can arise from the airways, the lung tissue or the pleura.
Q199.L2t: A pleural friction rub is produced when inflamed pleural surfaces rub together during breathing, and it is often accompanied by pleuritic chest pain.
Q199.L3t: A friction rub arises from the pleural surfaces moving against each other and is heard in both phases of breathing, often most prominently in expiration, whereas crackles arise from airways opening and are mainly inspiratory.
Q199.L4t: A crackling sound that is more prominent in expiration is more likely to be a pleural friction rub than crackles.
Q199.L2f: A pleural friction rub is caused by fluid-filled alveoli popping open and is never associated with chest pain.
Q199.L3f: Finger clubbing results from pleural inflammation, so its presence points to a pleural origin of the sound and away from crackles.
Q199.L4f: A crackling sound is more likely to be a pleural friction rub rather than crackles when clubbing is present.

Q200.L1t: Human cells are classified as either somatic cells or germ cells, and they differ in how many chromosomes they carry.
Q200.L2t: Human somatic cells are diploid, which means they carry two copies of each chromosome, one inherited from each parent.
Q200.L3t: Somatic cells contain 23 chromosomes from each parent, giving 23 pairs, and the total is twice the number found in a gamete.
Q200.L4t: All human somatic cells contain 46 chromosomes.
Q200.L2f: Human somatic cells are haploid and carry a single copy of each chromosome, with no pairs of homologous chromosomes.
Q200.L3f: Somatic cells are haploid, so they carry only the single set of chromosomes contributed by one parent and no second set.
Q200.L4f: All human somatic cells contain 23 chromosomes, so that is the correct answer.

Q201.L1t: Dehydration is a disturbance of fluid balance in which the body has lost more water, or water and salts, than it has taken in.
Q201.L2t: Hypernatraemia means a raised serum sodium concentration, and it is classified as a type of dehydration by the level of sodium in the blood.
Q201.L3t: In hypernatraemic dehydration the sodium concentration in the blood is high because the body has too little water relative to its sodium, which happens when the water taken in is not enough to replace the water lost.
Q201.L4t: Hypernatraemic dehydration is a state in which the water taken in is less than the body needs to stay in balance.
Q201.L2f: Hypernatraemic dehydration is diagnosed by a fall in serum sodium below the normal range of about 135 to 145 mmol/L.
Q201.L3f: Hypernatraemic dehydration arises when a person takes in excess water, which dilutes the body's sodium and so produces the raised sodium reading.
Q201.L4f: Hypernatraemic dehydration is a state in which the water taken in is greater than the body needs to stay in balance.

Q202.L1t: A peak flow meter is a hand-held device that measures the fastest speed at which a person can blow air out of the lungs.
Q202.L2t: Peak flow readings are normally taken as the best of three attempts, and the patient should use the same meter each time so that results can be compared.
Q202.L3t: Peak expiratory flow depends on how fully the chest and diaphragm can expand, and an upright posture gives the least restricted lung expansion, so readings are higher and more reproducible from one test to the next.
Q202.L4t: The patient should be upright because this allows the lungs to expand fully and gives readings that are accurate and consistent.
Q202.L2f: Peak flow meters should be calibrated by the patient before each reading, using a weight placed on the mouthpiece.
Q202.L3f: The main reason for the upright posture is practical rather than physiological: it puts the patient's mouth and chest in full view so that the clinician can watch each blow and check the technique, and lung expansion is largely unaffected by position.
Q202.L4f: The patient should be upright so that their technique can be easily observed by the person carrying out the test.

Q203.L1t: Intravenous therapy can lead to several local complications at the cannula site, and nurses are expected to check the site regularly for them.
Q203.L2t: Vesicant drugs, such as some chemotherapy agents, can destroy tissue when they escape from the vein, so they need especially careful administration and monitoring.
Q203.L3t: Of the terms listed, the one that specifically means leakage of a vesicant or irritant drug into the tissues around the vein is the one used when the damaging substance is a vesicant, whereas the terms for non-vesicant fluid leakage, for vein irritation and for a general tissue response do not carry this specific meaning.
Q203.L4t: The complication described is extravasation, which is the leakage of a vesicant medication into the surrounding tissues.
Q203.L2f: Complications at an IV site are rare because vesicant drugs are always given through large central veins, so they cannot leak into surrounding tissue.
Q203.L3f: The description refers to a general tissue response to irritation or injury, with redness, heat, swelling and pain at the site, and this response is the one that occurs when a vesicant drug leaks out, rather than a specific type of leakage.
Q203.L4f: The complication described is inflammation, which is the term for leakage of a vesicant medication into the surrounding tissues.

Q204.L1t: A stoma is a surgically created opening that brings bowel or urinary tract onto the abdominal wall so waste can leave the body.
Q204.L2t: Stomas such as colostomies, ileostomies and urostomies may be temporary or permanent depending on the underlying condition and the surgery performed.
Q204.L3t: Bowel resection for a malignant tumour often leaves no safe route for normal faecal passage, and cancer is among the leading indications for surgery that results in a stoma.
Q204.L4t: Cancer of the bowel or bladder is one of the most common reasons for a stoma to be formed.
Q204.L2f: Stomas are always permanent, and a temporary stoma is never used to let a surgical join in the bowel heal.
Q204.L3f: Irritable bowel syndrome causes structural damage to the bowel that commonly needs surgical resection, so it is a leading reason for stomas.
Q204.L4f: Irritable bowel syndrome is one of the most common reasons for a stoma to be formed.

Q205.L1t: Inhaled drugs act directly on the airways and need correct technique, because poor technique greatly reduces how much medicine reaches the lungs.
Q205.L2t: Much of the dose from a metered-dose inhaler can land in the mouth and throat, where it does not help the lungs.
Q205.L3t: Particles settle in the small airways by sedimentation when airflow stops, so a pause at the end of a slow, deep breath in lets the drug deposit there.
Q205.L4t: The patient should hold their breath after breathing in on using the inhaler, so the drug has time to settle in the lower airways.
Q205.L2f: Spacer devices raise the amount of drug that hits the throat, so they are not used for patients with poor coordination.
Q205.L3f: Rapid shallow breaths drive the drug particles deeper into the lungs, because fast repeated inhalations carry more aerosol past the upper airway.
Q205.L4f: Taking lots of small, quick breaths in is the way to get most of the drug into the lower airways.

Q206.L1t: Mitochondria are double-membrane organelles that produce most of a cell's ATP through aerobic respiration.
Q206.L2t: The mitochondrion has an outer membrane, an inner membrane folded into cristae, an intermembrane space and an inner matrix.
Q206.L3t: The proton gradient that drives ATP synthesis must be built across the inner membrane, so the carriers that pump protons are fixed within that membrane.
Q206.L4t: The inner mitochondrial membrane contains the protein complexes of the electron transport chain.
Q206.L2f: Mitochondria have a single membrane with no folds, and they are found only in cells that lack a nucleus.
Q206.L3f: Mitochondria are the main cellular site for storing energy reserves, so their inner membrane is packed with stored carbohydrate polymers.
Q206.L4f: Glycogen molecules are what is embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane.

Q207.L1t: Phosphocreatine is a high-energy phosphate compound that muscle cells use to store energy for short, intense efforts.
Q207.L2t: Phosphocreatine can donate its phosphate group to ADP to regenerate ATP quickly during the first seconds of intense exercise.
Q207.L3t: The enzyme creatine kinase and the phosphocreatine pool are soluble components that sit in the fluid part of the cell around the myofibrils, where ATP is used, rather than inside an organelle.
Q207.L4t: Phosphocreatine is found in the cytoplasm (sarcoplasm) of the muscle cell, dissolved in the cell fluid.
Q207.L2f: Phosphocreatine is made from the amino acids arginine, glycine and methionine, and its store in muscle is large enough to power maximal effort for several minutes.
Q207.L3f: Phosphocreatine is made and stored inside the organelle that carries out oxidative phosphorylation, so it is held within the double membrane of that organelle.
Q207.L4f: Phosphocreatine in the muscle cell is found in the mitochondria.

Q208.L1t: Many commonly prescribed drugs have side effects that affect the salivary glands, mouth or other parts of the digestive tract.
Q208.L2t: Dry mouth (xerostomia) is caused by reduced saliva flow and is a common side effect of medicines with anticholinergic activity.
Q208.L3t: Tricyclic antidepressants and some other antidepressants block muscarinic acetylcholine receptors, which reduces the parasympathetic stimulation of the salivary glands that normally drives saliva production.
Q208.L4t: Antidepressants are the group of drugs that may cause a dry mouth.
Q208.L2f: Dry mouth is mainly caused by excess fluid intake, which dilutes saliva and blocks the salivary glands from working properly.
Q208.L3f: Steroids suppress the salivary glands directly and strongly reduce saliva flow, so a dry mouth is their best-known and most frequent side effect.
Q208.L4f: Steroids are the group of drugs that may cause a dry mouth.

Q209.L1t: A stoma is an opening of the bowel brought out onto the abdominal wall, and its care requires appliances and sometimes extra accessories.
Q209.L2t: Surgical support garments and belts are designed to give gentle, even pressure over the abdominal wall around the stoma site.
Q209.L3t: A weakness in the abdominal wall muscle beside the stoma lets bowel push through, and a firm support garment helps by holding the abdominal wall in and stopping that bulge from growing.
Q209.L4t: A surgical support can be used for herniation around the stoma.
Q209.L2f: Surgical supports for stomas are always worn inside the stoma bag and must be changed every time the appliance is changed.
Q209.L3f: A prolapsed stoma is one where the bowel protrudes out through the stoma opening, and a firm external support pressing on the abdomen is the standard way to push it back and hold it in place.
Q209.L4f: A surgical support can be used for prolapsed stomas.

Q235.L1t: Pew Research surveys have long compared how religious belief is linked to views about morality across many countries.
Q235.L2t: The 2019 Pew survey asked people in many countries whether belief in God is necessary for being moral, and answers varied widely by country.
Q235.L3t: In the 2019 Pew survey, South Korea fell between the very secular, low-percentage Western European countries and the high-percentage countries of Africa and South Asia, with a figure clearly above one in four but below a majority.
Q235.L4t: Roughly four in ten South Koreans, a bit under half, said belief in God is necessary for morality.
Q235.L2f: The Pew survey on belief in God and morality was conducted only in Asian countries, and South Korea was the first country surveyed.
Q235.L3f: South Koreans are among the most secular people in the world, so only a small minority, about one in four, link belief in God to morality in the 2019 survey.
Q235.L4f: About a quarter of South Koreans said belief in God is necessary to be moral, so the lowest figure is the right one.

Q212.L1t: Bullying among adolescents has been measured by international organizations using school-based surveys in many countries.
Q212.L2t: Data on bullying of 13-15 year olds in Japan come from a 2015 international school survey asking about incidents in the previous couple of months.
Q212.L3t: The 2015 figure for Japan was well above the single-digit and low-teens rates but far below a majority, at a little over one in three students.
Q212.L4t: About thirty-six percent of Japanese children aged 13-15 said they had been bullied at least once in the past couple of months.
Q212.L2f: The 2015 Japan bullying data came from a survey of university students and asked only about bullying over the previous decade.
Q212.L3f: In Japan the 2015 survey showed a majority of students, around two in three, had been bullied recently, reflecting very high school bullying rates.
Q212.L4f: About two-thirds of Japanese children aged 13-15 reported being bullied at least once in the past couple of months, so the highest figure is right.

Q261.L1t: Life expectancy differs substantially across countries, shaped by income, health care, and public health conditions.
Q261.L2t: Life expectancy figures for 2019 for these four countries all fall between roughly the early 70s and the late 70s years.
Q261.L3t: In 2019 Brazil, China and Iran each had life expectancy a few years above Mexico's, which was held down by high rates of diabetes, obesity and violence-related deaths.
Q261.L4t: Mexico had the lowest life expectancy of the four countries in 2019.
Q261.L2f: In 2019 all four countries listed had life expectancy figures below 65 years because of widespread infectious disease.
Q261.L3f: Brazil's life expectancy in 2019 was a few years below that of Mexico, China and Iran, because of its much weaker health care and higher mortality overall.
Q261.L4f: Brazil had the lowest life expectancy of the four countries in 2019.

Q217.L1t: Tides are caused mainly by the gravitational pull of the Moon and, to a lesser extent, the Sun on Earth's oceans.
Q217.L2t: The Moon takes about 24 hours 50 minutes to return to the same position overhead, because it moves along its orbit while Earth rotates.
Q217.L3t: Most coasts get two high tides per lunar day, from tidal bulges on the near and far sides of Earth, so the gap between them is half of the roughly 24 hour 50 minute lunar day.
Q217.L4t: High tides come on average a little over twelve hours apart, about twelve and a quarter hours.
Q217.L2f: Tidal ranges are largest at neap tides, when the Sun and Moon pull at right angles to each other.
Q217.L3f: Each lunar day of about 24 hours 50 minutes contains roughly seven evenly spaced high tides, because the oceans form many bulges as Earth rotates.
Q217.L4f: The average gap between successive high tides is only a little over three hours.

Q266.L1t: Greenland is a self-governing territory within the Kingdom of Denmark, with a small population of about 56,000 people.
Q266.L2t: Greenland has long been reported to have one of the highest suicide rates in the world, especially among young Inuit men.
Q266.L3t: Greenland's suicide rate is about 60 per 100,000 people per year, while its overall death rate is roughly 850 per 100,000, so suicide makes up several percent of all deaths.
Q266.L4t: Suicide accounts for roughly one in fourteen deaths in Greenland, a little over seven percent.
Q266.L2f: Greenland's suicide rates are highest among elderly women, and young men are the group least affected.
Q266.L3f: Greenland's suicide rate is only about 8 per 100,000 per year, close to the European average, while its overall death rate is roughly 850 per 100,000.
Q266.L4f: Suicide accounts for less than one percent of all deaths in Greenland.

Q265.L1t: Economic growth is commonly measured as the percentage change in real average income per person over time.
Q265.L2t: Income growth in Britain during the industrial revolution was historically unprecedented but modest by modern standards, well under 2% per year.
Q265.L3t: Britain's average incomes grew at only about 1% per year during its industrial revolution, whereas less developed countries averaged around 2% per year over 1960 to 1995, roughly in line with the pace of rich countries.
Q265.L4t: Poorer countries' income growth over this period outpaced the rate Britain achieved during its industrial revolution.
Q265.L2f: Britain's industrial revolution began in the early twentieth century, after the First World War.
Q265.L3f: Between 1960 and 1995 average incomes in high income countries grew only about 1% per year, while less developed countries averaged around 4% per year.
Q265.L4f: Poorer countries' incomes grew faster than those of rich countries over this period, so they were catching up.

Q239.L1t: The Holocaust was the Nazi regime's systematic genocide of millions of Jews and others during World War II.
Q239.L2t: American pollsters such as Gallup and Roper surveyed public opinion on reports of Nazi atrocities against Jews while the war was still going on.
Q239.L3t: Polls taken in 1943 found that opinion was divided: fewer than a majority accepted the reports of mass murder, and a large minority dismissed them as rumor.
Q239.L4t: In 1943 about half of Americans believed that the Holocaust was happening.
Q239.L2f: The first national polls on Nazi atrocities were commissioned in 1939 by the Office of War Information and published in newspapers nationwide.
Q239.L3f: By 1943 extensive newspaper coverage had convinced a large majority of Americans, roughly seven in ten, that the extermination reports were true.
Q239.L4f: In 1943 about seven in ten Americans believed that the Holocaust was happening.

Q238.L1t: American foreign policy debates have long swung between active engagement abroad and restraint.
Q238.L2t: The term 'New Populism' came up in discussions of American attitudes toward foreign policy after the Cold War.
Q238.L3t: New Populism was a reaction against elite-driven global commitments, and it argued that domestic concerns should come before overseas involvement.
Q238.L4t: The New Populism was a strand of neo-isolationist sentiment.
Q238.L2f: The term 'New Populism' was coined in the 1930s to describe New Deal coalitions of farmers and industrial workers.
Q238.L3f: New Populism was built on the conviction that American values and culture were inherently better than others and should be the model for the world.
Q238.L4f: The New Populism was an expression of American cultural superiority.

Q316.L1t: The sum or product of integers has a parity that depends only on whether the integers involved are odd or even.
Q316.L2t: The expansion of a binomial raised to the sixth power follows the binomial theorem, with coefficients taken from a row of Pascal's triangle.
Q316.L3t: Each term is a binomial coefficient times a product of odd numbers, so a term is odd exactly when its coefficient is odd, and the coefficients are 1, 6, 15, 20, 15, 6, 1.
Q316.L4t: Four of the terms in the expansion are odd.
Q316.L2f: The coefficients in the expansion of a binomial to the sixth power come from a row of Pascal's triangle whose entries add up to 32.
Q316.L3f: A product of odd numbers is always odd, so every term in the expansion is odd, and the expansion has a term for every pair of exponents of m and n adding up to at most six.
Q316.L4f: Nine terms in the expansion are odd.

Q279.L1t: The Mean Value Theorem applies to functions that are continuous on a closed interval and differentiable on its interior.
Q279.L2t: The function f(x) = 2 sin x + sin 4x is continuous and differentiable everywhere, so the Mean Value Theorem applies on [0, π].
Q279.L3t: Since f(0) = f(π) = 0, the average rate of change is zero, so the points sought are the solutions of f'(x) = 2cos x + 4cos 4x = 0 in (0, π). Writing this as a quartic in t = cos x and checking its sign changes on [-1, 1] gives the number of roots.
Q279.L4t: The derivative equals the zero average slope at four distinct points of the interval.
Q279.L2f: The Mean Value Theorem requires the function to be a polynomial on the interval, and it guarantees exactly one point where the derivative equals the average slope.
Q279.L3f: Setting f'(x) = 0 reduces to a quadratic equation in cos x, and a quadratic has at most two roots, which limits the number of points.
Q279.L4f: The derivative equals the average rate of change at exactly two points of the interval.

Q326.L1t: Questions about perfect-square factors of an integer rely on its prime factorization and divisibility rules.
Q326.L3t: For n^2 to divide 2^4 · 3 · 5^2, n can contain 2 to at most the second power, 5 to at most the first power, and no factor of 3. That gives the n values 1, 2, 4, 5, 10 and 20, which can then be added.
Q326.L4t: The qualifying values of n add up to forty-two.
Q326.L2f: The number 1200 factors as 2^3 · 3 · 5^3, so it has fewer square factors than its size suggests.
Q326.L3f: The admissible values of n are only 1, 2, 4, 5, 10 and 17, because 20^2 = 400 does not divide 1200 evenly.
Q326.L4f: The qualifying values of n add up to thirty-nine.

Q294.L1t: Symbolizing English sentences in propositional logic means matching connective words like 'and', 'if', and 'unless' to truth-functional operators.
Q294.L2t: In the sentence, H stands for doctors being helpful and R stands for their patients being rude.
Q294.L3t: 'A unless B' means that if B is not the case, then A is, and the conditional ~B ⊃ A is truth-functionally equivalent to a disjunction of B with A.
Q294.L4t: The sentence is best symbolized as a plain disjunction of H and R.
Q294.L2f: In propositional logic, 'unless' is conventionally symbolized with the biconditional because it signals that the two clauses always share a truth value.
Q294.L3f: The word 'unless' requires both clauses to hold together, so the sentence asserts that doctors are helpful and patients are rude.
Q294.L4f: The sentence is best symbolized as the conjunction of H and R.

Q315.L1t: Rounding replaces a number with a nearby value at a chosen place value, and a digit of 5 or more in the next place rounds the digit up.
Q315.L2t: Rounding to a larger place value can move the result either up or down, depending on the digits that are dropped.
Q315.L3t: Rounding 12345.6789 gives 10000 at the ten-thousands place, 12000 at the thousands, 12300 at the hundreds and 12350 at the tens. Rounding to the nearest whole number or any decimal place gives about 12346 or less, so the largest result is the one from the tens place.
Q315.L4t: The person who rounds to the nearest ten gets the highest number, so that person wins.
Q315.L2f: When you round to a given place value, the digits after that place are always kept as they are and only the digit in that place changes.
Q315.L3f: Rounding to the nearest thousand turns 12345.6789 into 13000, because any digit after the thousands place pushes the thousands digit up.
Q315.L4f: The person who rounds to the nearest thousand ends up with the highest number, so that person wins.

Q295.L1t: A truth table lists every combination of truth values for the sentence letters and computes the truth value of each premise and the conclusion in every row.
Q295.L2t: An argument is invalid if and only if at least one row of its truth table makes every premise true and the conclusion false.
Q295.L3t: A conditional is true whenever its antecedent and consequent are both true, and a conjunction is true when both conjuncts are true. Q786.L3f: The Martian says he sat and watched the tiny glowing boxes in the big boxes, and that they were actual moving pictures to him, not television sets.
Q786.L4f: The Martian thinks the tiny glowing boxes are moving pictures.

Q731.L1t: The passage is about product safety problems in goods made in China and the reactions to them.
Q731.L2t: The passage says melamine was found in wheat flour used to make pet food sold in North America.
Q731.L3t: The passage names toxic medicine in Panama, toothpaste with the antifreeze chemical, melamine in pet food, restricted seafood imports and toys with lead paint, and a careful reader counts these distinct cases.
Q731.L4t: The passage mentions five cases of safety problems.
Q731.L2f: The passage says the pet food problem was caused by lead paint on the packaging and affected only cats in Europe.
Q731.L3f: The passage lists six separate safety cases because it counts the corruption case of the former drug agency head as a product safety problem of its own.
Q731.L4f: The passage mentions six cases of safety problems.

Q835.L1t: The letter is written by a visitor from Mars who describes the strange habits of life on Earth in a humorous way.
Q835.L2t: In the letter the Martian says that people leave their big boxes every morning and get into smaller boxes on wheels.
Q835.L3t: The Martian sees the small boxes race around and then stop to rest, and since he describes everything in terms of boxes, he is describing things with wheels that people ride in and park, which he sees as boxes with wheels in them.
Q835.L4t: The small boxes on wheels are the Martian's way of describing boxes that have wheels in them.
Q835.L2f: The letter says the Martian was angry about the football game and wrote to complain to the people who run the planet.
Q835.L3f: The Martian says the small boxes on wheels are body parts that people use to hear sounds while they race around and rest.
Q835.L4f: The small boxes on wheels are ears.

Q765.L1t: The passage is about apologies, forgiveness and healing between people, based on a talk by a spiritual researcher.
Q765.L2t: Caroline Myss says that saying "I never meant to hurt you" is not a sufficient apology, even though it may keep a friendship going.
Q765.L3t: After criticizing the weak apology, Myss redoes the scene and shows a soul-to-soul confession that admits knowing what you did and asks for forgiveness, which is a guide to the way to apologize that really heals.
Q765.L4t: The author's purpose is to tell people how to apologize sincerely.
Q765.L2f: Caroline Myss says that the phrase "I never meant to hurt you" is the best way to apologize and that it heals the other person's soul.
Q765.L3f: The passage spends almost all of its length listing the reasons why people are unable to say "I never meant to hurt you", and it offers no alternative way of speaking to the person who was hurt.
Q765.L4f: The author's purpose is to explain why people can't say "I never meant to hurt you".

Q738.L1t: A good title should sum up the main idea of the whole text rather than just one detail.
Q738.L2t: The study was led by Dr. Thomas Houston of the University of Massachusetts Medical School.
Q738.L3t: The whole text centers on one study of patients' recorded personal stories, and it reports lower blood pressure in those who watched them after three months and a lasting difference at six months.
Q738.L4t: The best title is the one saying that telling patients' stories can help bring blood pressure down.
Q738.L2f: Houston's team recruited all of its story-tellers from among the university's medical students.
Q738.L3f: The text mainly surveys the range of drug and lifestyle treatments for blood pressure, with the story study as only a passing example.
Q738.L4f: The best title is the one about medical treatments for blood pressure in general.

Q836.L1t: The text is a welcome message from a Swedish university promoting itself to prospective students.
Q836.L2t: The university says its popularity comes partly from the quality of its education and research and the range of courses it offers.
Q836.L3t: The text says the city has many theatres, concerts and festivals, which it describes as a rich and varied cultural life.
Q836.L4t: The statement that the cultural life is very rich is the true one.
Q836.L2f: The university describes itself as one of the smallest in Sweden and says it rarely attracts applicants.
Q836.L3f: The text says students are housed in the forests and recreation areas outside the city and live in the open air.
Q836.L4f: The statement that students can live outdoors is the true one.

Q857.L1t: The passage gives practical habits for falling asleep more easily.
Q857.L2t: The passage advises getting up and going to bed at the same time every day, even on weekends.
Q857.L3t: The passage says an empty stomach can disturb sleep but a heavy meal can too, so it recommends something light like warm milk.
Q857.L4t: It can be inferred that eating a small amount when very hungry before bed is fine.
Q857.L2f: The passage says naps are encouraged and should be taken in the evening for as long as possible.
Q857.L3f: The passage says occasional exercise at any hour, including just before bed, reliably helps people sleep.
Q857.L4f: It can be inferred that exercising now and then is what helps you sleep well.

Q734.L1t: The passage is a news-style article about brain training and how mental sharpness can decline in middle age.
Q734.L2t: The passage says Lumosity was designed by experts from Stanford University and is delivered through a Web-based program.
Q734.L3t: The author cites a study in which students gained 34 percent on math tests after six weeks, ahead of classmates who did not train, and uses that as evidence.
Q734.L4t: The author explains the training results by reporting what the studies and user reports found.
Q734.L2f: The passage says Lumosity was developed by a group of retired teachers and has been sold in stores for decades.
Q734.L3f: The passage lists regulations and step-by-step directions that readers must follow in order to get the training results.
Q734.L4f: The author explains the training results by laying down rules for readers to follow.

Q921.L1t: This is a criminal law question about offenses committed against people and property during a violent crime.
Q921.L2t: Robbery is the taking of property from a person by force or threat of force, and burglary is entering a dwelling with intent to commit a felony inside.
Q921.L3t: Under the felony murder rule, a death caused during the commission of a dangerous felony such as robbery or burglary is murder, even if it was unintended and came from the victim's own reaction.
Q921.L2f: Burglary requires that the defendant be armed and that the structure be a commercial building rather than a home.
Q921.L3f: The victim's own struggling is an independent intervening cause, and murder always requires proof that the defendant intended to kill, so the heart-attack death adds no liability.
Q921.L4t: The man is guilty of all three crimes: burglary, robbery, and murder under the felony murder rule.
Q921.L4f: The man is guilty of robbery and burglary only, because the heart attack death cannot be charged to him.

Q985.L1t: This is a torts question about the duty a landowner owes to people who come onto the land.
Q985.L2t: Under traditional tort law, the duty a possessor of land owes depends on the entrant's status, such as trespasser, licensee, or invitee.
Q985.L3t: A person is invited as a member of the public when the premises are held open to the public for a purpose, and a store restroom open to anyone who walks in is such a purpose.
Q985.L2f: Under traditional tort law, a landowner owes the same duty of care to every entrant regardless of status.
Q985.L3f: Anyone who enters a commercial store, whatever the reason, is treated as entering for a purpose connected with the owner's business dealings.
Q985.L4t: The jogger is an invitee who entered as a member of the public, since the store's bathroom was open to the public.
Q985.L4f: The jogger is a business visitor, because he entered a commercial store and used its facilities.

Q966.L1t: Property law governs the rights and duties of neighboring landowners with respect to one another's land.
Q966.L2t: Lateral support concerns the side-to-side support that adjoining land gives, while subjacent support concerns support from beneath the surface.
Q966.L3t: The sister's land subsided because of a structure the woman placed beneath its surface, and a landowner's right to have the surface held up from below is protected without regard to the builder's fault or care.
Q966.L4t: The sister should win because the woman's underground pipeline removed the support from beneath her land, and liability for that does not depend on negligence.
Q966.L2f: A landowner's right to have the land supported in its natural condition exists only if it was expressly granted in a written deed.
Q966.L3f: A landowner who builds an underground system is liable for resulting subsidence of a neighbor's land only when the construction was carried out carelessly.
Q966.L4f: The woman should prevail unless the sister can show that the woman built the drainage system carelessly.

Q899.L1t: The separation of powers divides authority among Congress, the President and the courts, and each branch has its own limits.
Q899.L2t: An appropriations statute provides funds for agency operations and is enacted through the formal process of bicameralism and presentment.
Q899.L3t: Only the text of an enacted statute binds the President, and legislators' unstated assumptions about how agencies will operate are not part of the statute.
Q899.L4t: The order is constitutional because no enacted law requires five-day operation and it concerns the internal management of the executive branch.
Q899.L2f: The Take Care Clause was added to the Constitution by the Twelfth Amendment.
Q899.L3f: The Constitution gives the operation of each agency's offices exclusively to the agency head, so the President has no power to set office hours.
Q899.L4f: The order is unconstitutional because agency heads, not the President, hold final responsibility for how their agencies' offices are run.

Q912.L1t: Criminal law defines each offense by specific elements, such as the required act and the required mental state.
Q912.L2t: At common law, robbery is the taking of property from a person or their presence by force or intimidation.
Q912.L3t: Completed robbery needs a taking caused by the victim's fear, but the owner was neither frightened nor deceived, and the woman still acted with the purpose of getting his money by threat.
Q912.L4t: The woman is guilty of attempted robbery, because she tried to take money by threat but the owner's lack of fear kept the robbery from being completed.
Q912.L2f: Common-law robbery requires that the property be taken from the victim's body rather than from the victim's presence.
Q912.L3f: False pretenses is complete whenever someone makes a false statement while getting money, even if the victim did not believe it.
Q912.L4f: The woman is guilty of false pretenses, because she obtained money by making a false statement about having a bomb.

Q925.L1t: Future interests such as executory interests are interests that take effect in possession only after some later event occurs.
Q925.L2t: An executory interest is a future interest held by a transferee that cuts short a preceding fee simple when a stated condition occurs.
Q925.L3t: The Greenacre condition could be triggered by anyone at any time in the indefinite future, so it might not vest within a life in being plus 21 years, whereas the Blackacre condition turns only on Associate's own conduct and must resolve within her lifetime.
Q925.L4t: Friend keeps Greenacre because Betty's executory interest in it is void under the Rule Against Perpetuities, while Betty takes Blackacre because her interest there is valid and Associate's drinking triggered it.
Q925.L2f: An executory interest is a type of reversion that always stays with the original grantor rather than passing to a third party.
Q925.L3f: The Rule Against Perpetuities does not apply to a gift over to the grantor's own heir, so both conditions are valid and both were triggered by the drinking.
Q925.L4f: Betty takes both Greenacre and Blackacre, because the drinking on each parcel triggered her executory interest.

Q933.L1t: The human mouth is home to bacteria, fungi, viruses and protozoa that live together as part of the body's normal flora.
Q933.L2t: The oral cavity has one of the most diverse microbial communities in the body, and many of its members live in biofilms such as dental plaque.
Q933.L3t: Culture-based and molecular surveys of the oral cavity have catalogued several hundred distinct microbial types, which is clearly more than a hundred but fewer than four hundred.
Q933.L4t: The mouth may be colonized by roughly three hundred and fifty different types of microorganisms.
Q933.L2f: Nearly all microbes in the mouth float freely in saliva and cannot attach to tooth surfaces or form biofilms.
Q933.L3f: Comprehensive surveys of the mouth have found only a modest total that tops out at one-tenth of a thousand types, and molecular methods have added essentially nothing to that count.
Q933.L4f: The mouth may be colonized by about one hundred different types of microorganisms.
